title: Evaluator CLI and Sidecar Plugin Spec
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary

This document defines the specification for the Evaluator CLI (evalctl) and the Sidecar Plugin Contract used by Redwood's eval harness. It formalizes command semantics, plugin manifest fields, telemetry expectations, failure modes, and rollout guidance for both hosted and private (dedicated/VPC) evaluator deployments. The goal is to enable consistent, auditable, and pluggable evaluators across teams and tenants while minimizing operational surprises during onboarding and mixed-precision/quant shadowing.

Goals
- Provide a single, stable CLI for running local, CI, and on-host evaluations.
- Define a minimal sidecar plugin API so third-party or customer-supplied evaluators can integrate with our shadow mesh.
- Surface required telemetry and artifact outputs for traceability, reproducibility, and automatic triage.
- Specify failure semantics and a safe rollback/stop mechanism for high-risk eval sweeps.

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: token-level and prompt-level evaluators, synthetic probe runners, function-call validators, and compact shadow probes.
- Non-goals: UI/Console integrations (visualization details live in product docs) and heavy-weight dataset catalog formats (these remain in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Terminology
- evalctl: the evaluator command-line tool consumed by CI, local dev, and on-host runners.
- sidecar plugin: an executable or HTTP service that implements the plugin contract to run evaluator workloads in a given environment.
- probe: a single test case or input used by an evaluator.

Contract overview
- Protocols supported: stdin/stdout JSON lines; HTTP/JSON REST (v1); and gRPC proto v1.
- Manifests: plugins must provide a plugin manifest file (YAML) describing capabilities, resource hints, and artifact outputs.
- Outputs: all evaluators must emit a standardized results envelope and an artifacts index.

Evaluator CLI (evalctl)
- Primary commands and semantics:
  1. evalctl init --manifest <path>: validates a plugin manifest and performs a dry-run capability test. Exit codes: 0=ok, 2=validation error, 3=permission/fatal.
  2. evalctl run --manifest <path> --workdir <dir> [--slice <slice-id>] [--mode local|ci|shadow] [--concurrency N] [--telemetry-level minimal|standard|verbose]
  3. evalctl collect --workdir <dir> --artifact-index out/index.json --output <s3://...|gs://...|local>
  4. evalctl stop --run-id <id> --graceful/--force

- Example usage:
  $ evalctl run --manifest ./plugin.yaml --workdir /tmp/eval-123 --mode shadow --concurrency 4
  $ evalctl collect --workdir /tmp/eval-123 --artifact-index out/index.json --output s3://eval-artifacts/tenant-a/2026-06-01

Plugin manifest (YAML) - minimal example
---
name: functional-reranker-evaluator
version: 0.3.1
protocols: ["stdin-jsonl", "http-json-v1"]
capabilities:
  - functioncall-validation
  - multiseed
resource_hints:
  cpu: "2"
  mem_mb: "4096"
  gpu: "0"
outputs:
  results_envelope: "results.jsonl"
  artifacts_index: "index.json"
telemetry_endpoint: "https://telemetry.redwood.internal/ingest"
health_check: "/healthz"
---

Fields explained
- name, version: semver used for promotion gating. New minor versions require in_review and a rollout plan.
- protocols: enumerates supported IPC forms. Plugins must support at least one protocol.
- capabilities: free-form tags that the eval mesh uses for routing (e.g., functioncall-validation, kv-cache-sensitive, quant-aware).
- resource_hints: best-effort hints used by the orchestrator for capacity decisions.
- outputs: relative file paths in the workdir that the plugin must produce. See "Outputs and artifact index" below.

Sidecar plugin API (HTTP JSON v1)
- Endpoints and expected payloads:
  GET /healthz -> 200 {"status":"ok","version":"0.3.1"}
  POST /run -> 202 Accepts a RunSpec JSON, returns {"run_id":"uuid-v4","eta_seconds": int}
  POST /stop -> 200 Accepts {"run_id": ... , "signal": "graceful|force"}
  GET /status?run_id=<id> -> 200 {"run_id":..., "state":"running|completed|failed|stopped","progress":0.0}
  GET /artifact-index?run_id=<id> -> 200 returns the artifacts index JSON file

RunSpec JSON (stringified example)
{
  "run_id": "string (optional, auto-generated)",
  "slice_id": "string",
  "probe_manifest": "s3://.../slice-manifest.json",
  "seeds": [42, 7, 2026],
  "mode": "shadow|ci|local",
  "telemetry_level": "minimal|standard|verbose",
  "max_examples": 10000
}

Outputs and artifact index
- Required artifact outputs (placed in workdir/out/<run_id>/):
  - results.jsonl (newline-delimited JSON with standardized ResultEnvelope)
  - index.json (artifact index described below)
  - optional: html-report.zip, debug-traces.tar.gz

Artifact index JSON (index.json) - required fields (stringified example)
{
  "run_id": "uuid",
  "started_at": "ISO8601",
  "completed_at": "ISO8601",
  "results_file": "results.jsonl",
  "summary": "out/summary.json",
  "checksums": {"results.jsonl":"sha256:..."},
  "telemetry_digest": "sha256:..."
}

ResultEnvelope (one per line in results.jsonl)
- Minimal fields: probe_id, input_hash, output_text, score (optional), metadata (map).
- Example line:
{"probe_id":"anchor-003","input_hash":"sha256:...","output_text":"...","score":0.87,"metadata":{"seed":42,"latency_ms":123}}

Telemetry and observability
- Required telemetry events:
  - eval.run.start (run_id, plugin_name, slice_id, mode)
  - eval.run.progress (run_id, percent, sampled_latency_ms)
  - eval.run.complete (run_id, result_counts, summary_metrics)
- Telemetry must include stable identifiers: run_id, plugin_name, tenant_id (when applicable), and slice_id.
- Minimum metrics reported at 1-minute granularity: examples_processed, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, failures_count.

Failure modes and remediation
- Validation errors (exit code 2): manifest or probe format is invalid. Remediation: fail-fast in CI; do not promote manifest.
- Runtime OOMs: plugin should write a tombstone file out/error_tombstone.json with reason and last N lines of stderr. Orchestrator will mark the run as failed and trigger an automated host-side capture.
- Silent drift (evaluation produces zero-length results): considered severity P1 for shadow runs. Automated triage will escalate to eval-oncall when the results rate < 1% of expected for two minutes.

Security and privacy constraints
- Sidecars operating on private deployments must honor tenant privacy: no telemetry outbound to hosted telemetry endpoints unless explicitly configured in the manifest and approved by privacy team.
- Artifacts containing PII must be encrypted at rest; index.json must include an encryption flag.

SLOs and gating for promotion
- Plugin correctness SLO for promoted validators: >= 99.5% successful runs on representative slices during a 72-hour shadow window.
- Performance SLO: median per-probe latency should be within 3x of the canonical evaluator for the same slice at promotion time.
- Safety gate: any run producing >0.5% hallucination-class failures on audited probes must block auto-promotion.

Onboarding checklist (required steps)
1. Create plugin manifest and commit to eval repo.
2. Run `evalctl init` locally and fix validation warnings.
3. Execute `evalctl run --mode local` on a representative slice and collect artifacts.
4. Submit a promotion request with telemetry links and artifacts.
5. Complete a 72-hour shadow run in the shadow mesh with `telemetry_level=standard` and provide the artifact index.
6. Product/ML reviewer and security reviewer sign-off.

Rollout and rollback procedure
- Canary rollout: 0.5% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with at least 1 hour steady-state per step for high-cost/nightly jobs.
- Rollback: `evalctl stop --run-id <id> --force` for active runs; remove manifest from routing tables and revert promotion tag.

Operational runbook (fast path)
1. Alert: "eval.run.rate-drop" triggers paging to eval-oncall.
2. Run `evalctl status` for top recent run_ids.
3. Pull artifacts: `evalctl collect --workdir /srv/eval/<run_id> --output /tmp/collect` and inspect out/error_tombstone.json.
4. If manifests were recently promoted, mark them as suspect in the promotion registry and roll back to previous version.

Ownership and contacts

- Runtime integration: Runtime Serving team (eng-serving-runtime).
- Observability contract: Eng Platform (dashboards-and-alerts).

Related pages and artifacts
- Evaluator certification curriculum (link above) contains the reviewer checklist referenced in the onboarding steps.
- Example plugin implementations live in repo: git://internal/redwood/eval-plugins (see README/plugin-examples).

Appendix A: Example CI job snippet
```yaml
jobs:
  eval-run:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run: evalctl init --manifest plugin.yaml
      - run: evalctl run --manifest plugin.yaml --workdir ./work --mode ci --concurrency 2
      - run: evalctl collect --workdir ./work --artifact-index ./work/out/index.json --output s3://eval-ci-artifacts/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}
      - run: curl -X POST $PROMOTION_ENDPOINT -d '{"artifact_index": "s3://..."}'
```

Appendix B: Example ergonomic debug workflow
- Developer: `evalctl run --mode local --concurrency 1 --telemetry-level verbose`
- If the plugin crashes, inspect workdir/out/error_tombstone.json, tail workdir/logs/plugin.stderr and open a ticket with copied artifacts and run_id.

Document history
- 2026-02-10: Draft created (Ava Martinez).
- 2026-04-01: Added telemetry digest requirement (Daniel Cho).
- 2026-06-12: Clarified artifact index and gated fields; moved security constraints to dedicated section (Priya Nair).

If you are implementing a new evaluator or integrating a third-party plugin, start with the manifest example and run `evalctl init`. For policy exceptions (exposing telemetry outbound from private deployments) contact security@redwood.internal with the exception request attached to the promotion ticket.
